engine_semantics.rule: Session.is_timed_out is time.monotonic() - last_active_time > timeout and is False when timeout is None; last_active_time is set when a session request is created (create_req), not when it finishes; maybe_reap closes a timed-out session unless it is streaming with an unfinished request
engine_semantics.consequence: the idle window is measured from the start of the session's last request, so the gap before a conversation's next turn (its own generation plus every other role's turn in between, including client retries) must fit inside it; no bound derived from the deadline covers that gap
engine_semantics.open_session_without_timeout: io_struct.OpenSessionReqInput.timeout defaults to None, so an /open_session body without timeout opens a session the scheduler never reaps

change.benchmarks/backends/sglang.py: open_history_session(session_id, timeout=600, *, expire_idle=True): expire_idle=False omits the engine timeout from the /open_session body; timeout still bounds the HTTP request; the default body is unchanged (same keys in the same order)

residual_risks: At the default 600 s deadline the historical 600 s session timeout remains, with the same latent gap: a turn gap above 600 s after a session request starts still reaps the session.
Without an idle timeout, a session outlives a proxy that is killed without its shutdown cleanup until the engine restarts or the next owner closes it; paper cells restart the engine per cell.

The persistent RACER adapter (experiments/history_system/runtime/benchmarks/memory_runtime/racer/generator.py) opens its session with the native request timeout as the idle timeout (10800 s by default, the paper deadline when one is configured) and is not changed here.
